account: Google switched on its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Greece on 28 April 2021. In Europe the system detects quakes with the accelerometers in phones and uses no seismographs. On 23 April 2025 the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck Türkiye. Google's team reports that the system detected it 5.31 seconds after it began and alerted more than 16 million users. Three weeks later, at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May), an earthquake struck between Kasos and Karpathos. The U.S. Geological Survey gives its magnitude as 6.0, and Greek outlets give 6.1. It was centered 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, at 76 km depth. The U.S. Geological Survey logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. On 14 and 15 May Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported that the system notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message and an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient or gives a lead time in seconds. None mentions damage or injuries. On 15 October 2026 Google extended the service to more than 200 regions.

ai_role.statement: If the reports are right, the alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake. Alerts were then pushed ahead of the slower waves, as Google's 2020 description and the 2025 Science paper set out. Google's own pages do not use the words AI or machine learning. The Science abstract speaks of smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The OECD Monitor classifies the system as AI doing event detection. That alerts arrived seconds before shaking rests on unattributed statements in four Greek outlets published within a day of the quake. None quotes a recipient, a seismologist or Google. No Google per-event confirmation was found.

fields.purpose: Built to detect earthquakes from the accelerometers of Android phones and combine the signals on Google's servers. It alerts users in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower seismic waves. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above. This alert was that intended function.

display.answer: Observed 14 May 2025. The quake struck at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May, per USGS), and the alerts went out seconds before the shaking. In.gr, writing on Thursday 15 May, places the quake in the early hours of Wednesday.

echoes.setting: M6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake, Türkiye; Google's team reports that the system detected the quake 5.31 seconds after it began and alerted more than 16 million users (Mousavi et al., Nature Communications, 2026; authors are Google staff).

must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports that only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. The Greek reports document no protective action by anyone who received the alert.
The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts). The feature must be supported in the region.
produced_by: A magnitude 6.0 (USGS) quake above the system's 4.5 alert threshold, centered offshore south of Kasos at about 76 km depth. A push alert could therefore outrun the slower waves to Crete and the Dodecanese.

Enough Android phones near the epicentre with the Earthquake Alerts setting on to trigger Google's server-side detection. In Europe the system uses the accelerometers in phones instead of seismographs (in.gr).
Receiving phones with location (GPS) enabled and an internet connection, which Alphafreepress lists as requirements for the alerts

fields.account: Google switched on its Android Earthquake Alerts System in Greece on 28 April 2021. In Europe the system detects quakes with the accelerometers in phones and uses no seismographs. On 23 April 2025 the magnitude 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck Türkiye. Google's team reports that the system detected it 5.31 seconds after it began and alerted more than 16 million users. Three weeks later, at 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May), an earthquake struck between Kasos and Karpathos. The U.S. Geological Survey gives its magnitude as 6.0, and Greek outlets give 6.1. It was centered 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, at 76 km depth. The U.S. Geological Survey logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. On 14 and 15 May Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported that the system notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message and an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient or gives a lead time in seconds. None mentions damage or injuries. On 15 October 2026 Google extended the service to more than 200 regions.
fields.summary: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System warned Android users in Crete and the Dodecanese seconds before a magnitude 6.0 quake near Kasos on 14 May 2025.
